text: sqlpipe moves rows from Postgres to S3 as Parquet files. The system has three processes. The reader connects to Postgres and streams rows in batches. Each batch holds a fixed number of rows. The reader sends each batch to the converter. The converter turns each batch into one Parquet row group. The converter groups rows by column to reduce the file size. The converter sends finished row groups to the uploader. The uploader writes the row groups to S3 as a multipart upload. Each part is one object segment. If a part upload fails, the uploader retries the part. The uploader retries each part up to a fixed limit. The three processes run at the same time. This design keeps memory use low because no process holds the full result set.
